fullPassage:
Analogies can serve two different functions in philosophy. Sometimes, as seems often the case in Plato, for example, they serve simply to illustrate. When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may simply be using the image of the sun to help bring to life his arguments about the Good. On other occasions, however, the analogy can be an integral part of an argument. Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley. The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so the universe implies the existence of a divine creator. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point. Rather, the analogy is supposed to show why we should conclude that the universe has a creator.

* analogy: 유추 ** theologian: 신학자 *** artisan: 장인

det.analysis: 조동사 may 뒤에서 동사구 'be using'을 수식하려면 부사가 필요. 형용사 simple을 부사 simply로 변환. 'may simply be using'(단순히 사용하고 있을 수 있다)
det.tip: 부사가 동사구 수식: simply(부사) + be using(동사). simple(형용사) → simply(부사)

overlay.excerptSentences: When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may __________ (simple) be using the image of the sun to help bring to life his arguments about the Good.

questions.passage: Analogies can serve two different functions in philosophy. Sometimes, as seems often the case in Plato, for example, they serve simply to illustrate. When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may simply be using the image of the sun to help bring to life his arguments about the Good. On other occasions, however, the analogy can be an integral part of an argument. Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley. The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so __________. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point. Rather, the analogy is supposed to show why we should conclude that the universe has a creator.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① the watch needs a new design: 시계의 새 디자인은 논증과 무관
❌ ② philosophy requires more analogies: 더 많은 유추 필요성은 논증 내용이 아님
✅ ③ the universe implies the existence of a divine creator: 시계-장인 유추에 대응하여 우주-창조자를 연결 ← 정답
❌ ④ Socrates compared the Good with the sun: 소크라테스의 비유는 설계 논증이 아닌 다른 사례
det.tip: just as A, so B 구문: 시계→장인 = 우주→창조자

questions.passage: Analogies can serve two different functions in philosophy. Sometimes, as seems often the case in Plato, for example, they serve simply to illustrate. When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may simply be using the image of the sun to __________. On other occasions, however, the analogy can be an integral part of an argument. Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley. The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so the universe implies the existence of a divine creator. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point. Rather, the analogy is supposed to show why we should conclude that the universe has a creator.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① prove that the sun is the ultimate Good: 태양이 궁극적 선이라는 증명은 본문 내용이 아님
✅ ② help bring to life his arguments about the Good: 선에 대한 논증을 생생하게 만들기 위해 태양 이미지를 사용 ← 정답
❌ ③ disprove the existence of a divine creator: 창조자 부정은 소크라테스의 태양 비유와 무관
❌ ④ replace philosophical reasoning with imagery: 철학적 추론을 대체가 아니라 보조하는 것
det.tip: bring to life = 생생하게 만들다. 태양 이미지로 선에 대한 논증을 생생하게 표현
